boundaries: Coverage is a semantic criterion, not a Measurement Method, Measurement Result, Finding or Decision.
An admitted meaning would govern only its exact scope; it grants no agent permission.
A fixed account and filters identify the required population, but this coverage predicate does not itself forbid extra account records.
Changing an application to a different snapshot requires a new evidence comparison; changing the normative meaning requires a new Definition version.
claim_ceiling: Proposed Definition/v2 mapping specimen. No definition admission, source promotion, accepted incident finding, consumer adoption, agent permission or incident closure is asserted.

scope.applicability: A proposed shared identifier-coverage criterion for Lab export investigations with fixed, identified S, A, F and E and an established required identifier population. It does not assert an external customer policy.
exclusions: Account exclusivity, extra identifiers and unauthorized disclosure.
Permission to run extraction, repair production, or close an incident.

source_refs.selector: whole exact governing Definition record; structure and authority boundary only

examples: The missing-ID fixture fails identifier coverage.
A retry containing all 12,000 required IDs passes coverage; the incident still needs its independent accuracy, exclusivity and closure reviews.
A file with 12,000 rows but 200 duplicates replacing required IDs still fails coverage.
domain_context.explanation: The agent investigates INC-1042 using saved S-1042, the Northstar account, status=active filters and E-1042. The synthetic missing-ID case has 12,000 required identifiers and 11,800 unique exported identifiers, leaving 200 missing. This applies the proposed criterion and does not establish an actual production finding.

plain_language.explanation: Every required row identifier for the chosen account, filters and snapshot must appear in the saved output.

boundary_conditions: The required population must be established; an unknown population is not an empty set.
Use the same fixed snapshot, account and filter semantics in the expected population and export comparison.
A genuinely established empty required set satisfies the coverage criterion.
Extra identifiers, duplicate rows, inaccurate values, and closure decisions require separate criteria.
scientific_formal.normative_statement: For a fixed source snapshot S, declared account A, declared filters F and saved output E, export identifier completeness holds exactly when every identifier required by S, A and F appears in E.

notation.meaning: The declared account whose records are required.
The declared filters evaluated against S within A.
The established set of identifiers required by S, A and F.
The set of identifiers actually present in E; multiplicity is ignored.
Every member of the required set appears in the exported set; equality and absence of extras are not asserted.

testable_conditions: Every required identifier present implies CompleteIds=true.
One missing required identifier implies CompleteIds=false.
Equal row counts with duplicate IDs can still fail identifier completeness.
All required IDs with inaccurate values pass coverage while accuracy can fail.
Without an established required population, the criterion is not evaluable.
